## Problem

/mcp can return persistent HTTP 502 after concurrent gate load if nginx's single-server upstream points at a dead MCP container. Parent witted-invisible-roan made autodeploy retain a crashed live backend instead of deleting it, but recovery can still wait for Docker/humans.

## RCA / design decision

Related load-side ticket enduring-ironclad-arrowana already removed the biggest measured retained-memory multiplier: retained plan-review snapshot state fell from 256,646,460 bytes to 37,046 bytes on a 9,081-ticket store. This ticket fixes the serving-path residue.

Selected prevention: an autodeploy in-place watchdog for the live MCP backend. On each serialized autodeploy tick (the existing flock owns check/start/readiness/backoff), MCP_SELF_HEAL defaults to 1 inside autodeploy.sh so the fix is active after merge; setting it to 0 is the kill switch. The watchdog uses the existing MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT readiness deadline. If MCP_SELF_HEAL=1 and the nginx upstream port maps to a managed MCP container that is not running, autodeploy runs docker start on the live container and readiness-checks that same port. A healthy running backend is a strict no-op. The port-to-container lookup must work for exited containers using inspect data, not docker port alone. Success leaves nginx byte-identical, clears MCP backoff, and logs recovery; failure leaves the container/upstream identity intact, emits existing AUTODEPLOY_ERROR mcp-live-backend-down, records MCP backoff, and remains a retryable transient path; repeated backoff cycles are the operator escalation signal for a fatal start/config problem. Active MCP backoff is honored before retrying so repeated ticks do not hammer Docker. MCP_SELF_HEAL=0 disables the new branch and restores log-and-wait behavior.

Rejected alternatives: blue/green self-heal doubles MCP memory under pressure; nginx passive failover needs an already-live spare; Docker restart always is already present but is passive and not readiness/log evidenced; healthcheck watchdog/autoheal prior art supports this design and is implemented here through the existing autodeploy tick instead of a new daemon; instance sizing/off-box gates remain with inherited-americium-porpoise.

## Testing / verification plan

- RED/GREEN tests in tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py: no source change pending, nginx points at an exited managed MCP backend, one tick runs docker start for that exact container, upstream remains unchanged, success log appears, and readiness passes.
- RED/GREEN tests for failure/kill switch/backoff: failed start or readiness does not remove the dead live backend, upstream remains unchanged, AUTODEPLOY_ERROR mcp-live-backend-down and deploy_failed wiring appear, MCP backoff is recorded, active backoff skips restart, and MCP_SELF_HEAL=0 skips restart.
- RED/GREEN tests for source-advancing ticks and exited-container port lookup: the watchdog runs before the ordinary blue/green deploy path, and the Docker stub only returns docker port for running containers so the docker inspect HostConfig.PortBindings fallback covers exited live containers.
- Verified locally: bash -n infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh, pytest -q tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py (61 tests), make lint, and env-sanitized make verify.
- Live check after merge: no Terraform apply is required because failure visibility reuses existing deploy_errors wiring and success is operator-visible journald evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The selected design is recorded with why alternatives were accepted/rejected.
- [x] A simulated MCP backend death recovers without persistent nginx 502.
- [x] The prevention is covered by tests and visible through existing deploy-error alarm wiring plus logs.
- [x] [non-codebase] Capacity/concurrency measurements cite enduring-ironclad-arrowana and the residual campaign inherited-americium-porpoise.
  provenance: environment=rebar-ticket-store; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — cited ticket comments and Gerrit 2807 evidence are tracker/Gerrit artifacts, not repository source files.
